rules.title: Xcode build files
rules.whatItIs: Build results and indexes Xcode creates for your projects.
rules.consequence: Every project will rebuild and re-index in full the next time you open it.
rules.sideCondition: Quit Xcode and any builds. Delete the contents, not the folder.

rules.title: Xcode archives
rules.whatItIs: Saved builds of apps you shipped, with their debugging symbols.
rules.consequence: You would lose the ability to read crash reports for those builds or re-export them.
rules.sideCondition: Review each archive by date and version. Move to Trash only.

rules.title: Device support files
rules.whatItIs: Debugging symbols Xcode copied from a connected iPhone, iPad or watch.
rules.consequence: Xcode copies them again the next time you connect that device, which is slow, and old crash logs lose their symbols until then.
rules.sideCondition: Delete the folders inside, never the parent. Keep the newest two versions. Close Xcode first.

rules.title: Simulator devices
rules.whatItIs: A simulated iPhone or iPad with its installed apps and test data.
rules.consequence: You would lose the apps and test data inside that simulator.
rules.sideCondition: Do not delete by hand. The command removes only simulators whose runtime is gone.

rules.title: Simulator runtimes
rules.whatItIs: The system images that simulators run on.
rules.consequence: You would need to download the runtime again, which can be several gigabytes.
rules.sideCondition: Remove through Xcode Settings or the runtime commands, never by hand or by unmounting.

rules.title: Xcode settings
rules.whatItIs: Your Xcode snippets, themes and key bindings.
rules.consequence: You would lose settings you wrote yourself.
